project.name: Worth Store S.7.1 Proof-Flow And Domain-Structure Cleanup Gate

phases.title: Structural Inventory And Concept Freeze
phases.owner: `worth-store` cleanup gate across critical Store crates
acceptance: Inventory names critical root-file, facade, wildcard-export, mod.rs, helper-placement, copied-constructor, and overloaded-function cleanup targets.
Inventory classifies each finding by structural failure mode and evidence needed for closeout.
No new Store concept expansion is planned as part of the inventory.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 1. Produce the cleanup map that later phases consume. Treat this as structural evidence work, not feature implementation.
phases.qa_focus: Check that the inventory identifies root architectural failure modes rather than surface ugliness, and that it preserves the concept freeze.

phases.title: Certification Courtroom Cleanup
acceptance: Production law needed by Store crates lives in production crates rather than certification-only vocabulary.
Certification surfaces are named and structured as evidence, replay, scenario, courtroom, or harness authority.
Changed construction boundaries have appropriate mechanical evidence.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 2. Clean certification so it proves and replays Store law without becoming the law.
phases.qa_focus: Check for certification-as-law, production crates depending on certification rows, and test authority that can mint production proof.

phases.title: Physical Format Topology Cleanup
acceptance: Physical-format skeleton is organized by stable artifact responsibility and lifecycle.
`lib.rs`, facades, and aggregation modules aggregate rather than implement business logic.
Raw construction boundaries are sealed or documented with focused evidence where changed.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 3. Clean the physical-format topology before S.8 layout work inherits it.
phases.qa_focus: Check for flat roots, broad lib.rs logic, exported topology, and raw format construction seams.

phases.title: Blob Crate Lifecycle Tree
acceptance: Blob crate skeleton teaches identity, lifecycle, streaming, publication, recovery, reachability, placement, compaction, corruption, counters, and test support responsibilities.
Root file count and module depth match the declared lifecycle tree or carry a narrow exemption.
Helper/test-support placement follows the narrowest responsibility it serves.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 4. Reshape the blob crate from ontology dump into lifecycle tree.
phases.qa_focus: Check for same-level file swamps, vague helper homes, mixed classification axes, and god modules.

phases.title: Blob Public Facade And Export Grammar
acceptance: Public facade shape teaches valid blob lifecycle order and authority class.
Public exports are narrower than internals and no longer mirror accidental topology.
Changed proof-object construction boundaries have mechanical evidence.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 5. Shape public exports around lifecycle capabilities and authority, not alphabet soup.
phases.qa_focus: Check for ontology dump exports, public raw constructors, deep import pressure, and facades that hide lifecycle order.

phases.title: Chunk Identity And Dedupe Proof Grammar
acceptance: Dedupe flow has named evidence collection, classification, verification, receipt/counter construction, and next capability.
Digest equality is represented as evidence within admitted security scope rather than authority by itself.
Overloaded dedupe functions are decomposed into auditable semantic steps.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 6. Clean chunk identity and dedupe into explicit proof grammar.
phases.qa_focus: Check for digest-only authority, copied receipt fields, counter decoration, hidden collision policy, and god functions.

phases.title: Publication, WAL, And Recovery Proof Grammar
acceptance: Publication/recovery state graph is visible in code and public capability flow.
Partial publication, WAL evidence, replay admission, and visible authority are distinct states.
Overloaded publication/recovery functions are decomposed into named transition steps.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 7. Clean publication, WAL, and recovery proof grammar without adding new blob behavior.
phases.qa_focus: Check for boolean publication state, recovery records as alternate authority, copied recovery ids, and mixed visibility states.

phases.title: Streaming Ingest, Read, And Resume Proof Grammar
acceptance: Streaming loop shape separates admission, frontier advancement, chunk-window verification, memory counters, and receipt construction.
Constant-memory evidence remains visible at transition boundaries touched by cleanup.
Streaming functions read as orchestration plus named semantic steps.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 8. Clean streaming proof grammar and overloaded streaming loops.
phases.qa_focus: Check for whole-object materialization pressure, stale resume authority, mixed read/write authority, and hidden counter updates.

phases.title: Reachability, Retention, And Reclaim Proof Grammar
acceptance: Reachability/reclaim decision table is named and auditable.
Reference, retention, recovery, dedupe, and security-scope authorities remain distinct.
Counters and receipts attach to classified reclaim outcomes.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 9. Clean reachability, retention, and reclaim proof grammar.
phases.qa_focus: Check for generic reference rows, orphan-looking chunk shortcuts, hidden horizon checks, and reclaim god functions.

phases.title: Placement, Movement, And Compaction Proof Grammar
acceptance: Placement/movement state graph identifies stable-read, security scope, and I/O admission evidence.
Movement receipts expose the next valid capability without treating placement as semantic validity.
Compaction and movement functions are decomposed into named transition steps.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 10. Clean placement, movement, and compaction proof grammar.
phases.qa_focus: Check for movement as metadata rewrite, scheduler admission as semantic proof, backend residue authority, and mixed placement states.

phases.title: Corruption, Quarantine, And Readmission Proof Grammar
acceptance: Corruption/quarantine/readmission decision table is explicit before logical decode.
Checksum failure, authenticity failure, missing chunk, stale generation, and cross-scope import remain distinct cases.
Quarantine receipts expose diagnostics and repair/readmission capability rather than ordinary read authority.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 11. Clean corruption, quarantine, and readmission proof grammar.
phases.qa_focus: Check for generic corruption errors, readmission from terminal declarations, quarantine as ordinary read proof, and decode-before-damage classification.

phases.title: Recovery, Isolation, Scheduler, And Backend Seam Cleanup
acceptance: Each touched lower seam clearly owns its production law.
Blob and certification code adapt to lower seam capabilities rather than copying lower proof fields.
Cross-crate handoffs are sealed or phase-typed where proof crosses crate boundaries.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 12. Clean adjacent Store seams that support blob proof flow.
phases.qa_focus: Check for copied counters/receipts/proof ids, scheduler-as-semantic-proof, dependency inversion, and S.7 helpers leaking into lower crates.

phases.title: Buffer Pool And Physical Integrity Targeted Cleanup
acceptance: Blob-adjacent memory and integrity cleanup preserves visible resident-byte/allocation and corruption-first evidence.
Integrity classification remains before logical decode.
Any shared helpers preserve identical authority and lifecycle or remain local.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 13. Clean only buffer-pool and physical-integrity surfaces that affect proof-flow readability, memory bounds, or corruption-first behavior.
phases.qa_focus: Check for hidden allocation, page clone pressure, whole-object residency, generic helpers, and decode-before-integrity classification.

phases.title: Test And Certification Topology Cleanup
acceptance: Test support topology identifies production-facade users and named test authority.
Synthetic certification authority is labeled as courtroom evidence rather than production proof.
Helper construction boundaries have mechanical evidence where changed.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 14. Clean test and certification topology so it falsifies production topology rather than bypassing it.
phases.qa_focus: Check for test helpers minting impossible production authority, generic fixture worlds, unclear synthetic evidence, and helper swamps.

phases.title: Structural Closeout And S.8 Readiness
acceptance: Closeout bundle shows cleaned Store crates satisfy file-count, aggregation, facade visibility, construction-boundary, and S.7 hostile-lane evidence appropriate to touched surfaces.
S.8 can consume blob/layout inputs through cleaned S.7/S.7.1 capabilities rather than raw blob internals, copied counters, certification rows, or helper constructors.
Remaining structural exceptions, if any, have explicit reason, owner, scope, and follow-on milestone.
phases.instructions: Implement S.7.1 Phase 15. Produce the structural closeout and S.8 readiness evidence for this cleanup gate.
phases.qa_focus: Check that the milestone is actually ready to hand S.8 a cleaned topology and proof grammar, not just a partially reorganized blob crate.
